questions.question: A preferred /32 route stays active after its fixed next-hop stops forwarding, while a backup route exists. Which change makes route installation depend on peer liveness?

choices.text: Increase the backup route administrative distance
choices.feedback: Distance only ranks routes; it does not detect a failed next-hop.

choices.text: Enable BFD on the primary static route
choices.feedback: The route itself must be BFD-enabled so a Down session withdraws it.

choices.text: Enable interface ping monitoring only
choices.feedback: Ping monitoring may alert, but it does not bind withdrawal to this route.

choices.text: Redistribute the route into OSPF
choices.feedback: Redistribution advertises routes; it does not supply static-route liveness.

questions.question: BFD reports the preferred neighbor Up, but the expected destination is absent from the routing table. What should be checked next?

choices.text: Lower the BFD detection multiplier again
choices.feedback: Timer tuning does not explain a missing route when the session is already Up.

choices.text: Inspect the static route destination, gateway and distance
choices.feedback: A live BFD session does not prove the destination prefix is installed or preferred.

choices.text: Enable BFD echo mode on both peers
choices.feedback: FortiGate does not support BFD echo mode.

choices.text: Change the backup route to equal distance
choices.feedback: Equal distance changes path selection but does not correct a missing prefix.

questions.question: A default route exits through an SD-WAN zone with dynamic member selection. Which health mechanism fits this design?

choices.text: Use an SD-WAN Performance SLA for member health
choices.feedback: Performance SLAs evaluate individual SD-WAN members and remove unhealthy members from selection.

choices.text: Create a fixed neighbor under router BFD
choices.feedback: A neighbor entry alone does not bind health to dynamic zone members.

choices.text: Raise the static route distance on every member
choices.feedback: Distance changes do not measure path quality or member liveness.

choices.text: Bind BFD to the SD-WAN zone default route
choices.feedback: A zone does not provide one fixed next-hop for route-bound BFD.

questions.question: BFD changes to Down and the backup route becomes active, but users still cannot reach the application. What does the next test target?

choices.text: Review device-wide BFD settings before testing the path
choices.feedback: Global BFD settings do not establish application reachability through the backup.

choices.text: Recheck BFD timer negotiation on the failed peer
choices.feedback: The route has already changed; timer tuning does not establish whether the backup path forwards.

choices.text: Inspect the primary interface's administrative state only
choices.feedback: Interface state alone does not prove the backup route forwards correctly.

choices.text: Test the backup gateway, route and application path
choices.feedback: The BFD state transition is already evidenced by the route withdrawal; now prove the backup path forwards end to end.

questions.question: A first policy-package install removes local FortiGate address objects that are not currently referenced. What import control best prevents this?

choices.text: Enable Add ALL Objects when importing the configuration
choices.feedback: Add ALL Objects preserves the broader object inventory in Policy & Objects.

choices.text: Create a new policy package with no install targets
choices.feedback: A package without targets cannot reconcile the device configuration.

choices.text: Disable default object mapping for the ADOM
choices.feedback: Missing mappings cause install failures; they do not preserve local objects.

choices.text: Convert the device to a model device first
choices.feedback: Model-device conversion is unrelated to importing unreferenced objects.

questions.question: The Install Wizard fails because an address object has no target-specific value. Which dependency should be corrected?

choices.text: The package installation preview theme
choices.feedback: Preview appearance does not determine object value resolution.

choices.text: Default or per-device object mapping
choices.feedback: FortiManager requires default or per-device mapping for mapped objects.

choices.text: The ADOM administrator's dashboard layout
choices.feedback: Dashboard layout has no effect on installation mapping.

choices.text: The FortiGate's local DNS resolver
choices.feedback: DNS resolution is not the missing object-mapping dependency.

questions.question: Before the first managed install, an engineer wants to review the exact proposed delta without changing the FortiGate. What should be used?

choices.text: A policy package export after installation
choices.feedback: An export after installation is too late to review the proposed delta.

choices.text: A direct CLI script on the FortiGate
choices.feedback: Direct CLI execution changes the device outside the package preview workflow.

choices.text: The Install Wizard installation preview
choices.feedback: The preview exposes proposed changes and can be cancelled before modification.

choices.text: The FortiGate event log after reboot
choices.feedback: A post-reboot log cannot replace a pre-install preview.

questions.question: A change should install only the interface policy, not the broader device settings. Which Install Wizard choice matches that scope?

choices.text: Install the entire ADOM database
choices.feedback: An ADOM database is not a device installation target.

choices.text: Install interface policy only
choices.feedback: The interface-policy-only option is the narrower documented install scope.

choices.text: Install policy package and device settings
choices.feedback: The broader operation includes ADOM/policy-layer and device-layer settings.

choices.text: Run a remote CLI script instead
choices.feedback: A direct script is a separate execution path, not the interface-policy install option.

questions.question: An analyst needs combined Log View and reports from FortiGate and FortiSandbox in one analysis context. What ADOM type is required?

choices.text: A per-device private ADOM
choices.feedback: Separate private ADOMs keep the devices in different analysis contexts.

choices.text: A Security Fabric ADOM
choices.feedback: Fabric ADOMs combine supported Security Fabric devices across analysis panes.

choices.text: A FortiManager global database ADOM
choices.feedback: FortiManager's global database is not a FortiAnalyzer ADOM type.

choices.text: A backup-mode ADOM
choices.feedback: Backup mode is not the cross-product analysis boundary.

questions.question: Converting an existing non-Fabric ADOM with the documented migration command has which operational consequence?

choices.text: It only refreshes the Log View browser tab
choices.feedback: A browser refresh does not perform ADOM type migration.

choices.text: It moves devices without affecting service state
choices.feedback: The migration is a system operation with a reboot, not a live cosmetic move.

choices.text: It restarts the FortiAnalyzer system
choices.feedback: The documented migration displays affected ADOMs and reboots the system.

choices.text: It changes the FortiGate firmware automatically
choices.feedback: FortiAnalyzer ADOM migration does not upgrade FortiGate firmware.

questions.question: FortiAnalyzer shows no allowed web-filter logs for a device. The same time range has no matching records in Archive. What is the first conclusion?

choices.text: The GUI filter hides the selected log subtype
choices.feedback: A GUI filter can hide a view, but the Archive check for the same device and time range is already empty.

choices.text: The Fabric ADOM is missing from the report dataset
choices.feedback: ADOM membership affects analysis scope, but it cannot explain an empty Archive.

choices.text: The ClickHouse rebuild is still processing older partitions
choices.feedback: A rebuild affects Analytics data; it does not explain why raw Archive logs are absent.

choices.text: FortiGate did not generate or forward those logs
choices.feedback: FortiAnalyzer processes received logs; an empty Archive points upstream to source logging or forwarding.

questions.question: After a 7.4-to-7.6 upgrade, Analytics disk usage drops sharply, but the oldest date and daily counts still match retention. What is the right interpretation?

choices.text: Start a full Analytics rebuild before checking data
choices.feedback: A rebuild is a recovery operation for verified missing data and reboots the appliance.

choices.text: ClickHouse compression can reduce disk use
choices.feedback: ClickHouse is columnar and compresses data; disk usage alone is not a completeness test.

choices.text: Treat the smaller database as proof of data loss
choices.feedback: A smaller database alone does not prove missing data; compare dates and per-day counts.

choices.text: Increase the Analytics quota before checking Archive
choices.feedback: Quota is a retention dependency, but the stated dates and counts already match retention.

questions.question: IGMP snooping lists a receiver port, but a source-specific stream cannot cross VLANs. What is missing?

choices.text: Increase MAC aging for the receiver VLAN
choices.feedback: MAC aging affects unicast forwarding state, not the multicast routing tree.

choices.text: Configure the SSM flow on a PIM-enabled routed SVI
choices.feedback: Snooping is Layer 2; routed SSM needs the source/group flow and a PIM-enabled SVI.

choices.text: Create a second snooping table for that VLAN
choices.feedback: A second snooping table still does not provide inter-VLAN PIM routing.

choices.text: Add a static ARP entry for the receiver host
choices.feedback: Static ARP does not establish IGMPv3 membership or PIM forwarding.

questions.question: A design requires PIM routing and an IGMP querier on the same SVI. What should the engineer change?

choices.text: Raise querier priority on that same SVI
choices.feedback: Priority does not remove the documented same-SVI feature conflict.

choices.text: Disable snooping across the entire switch fabric
choices.feedback: Snooping is independent and does not resolve the PIM/querier conflict.

choices.text: Enable both and lengthen the query interval
choices.feedback: Changing the interval cannot override the documented same-SVI restriction.

choices.text: Choose one function for that SVI and redesign membership
choices.feedback: The guide forbids PIM and an IGMP querier on the same SVI; separate the functions or choose one.

questions.question: PIM configuration is present but the advanced-features license is absent. What is the first corrective action?

choices.text: Enable BFD for the multicast neighbor
choices.feedback: BFD is not supported for this PIM function.

choices.text: Tune the PIM hello interval to one second
choices.feedback: Hello tuning cannot enable a licensed feature.

choices.text: Add a route-map to the SVI
choices.feedback: Route maps are not supported by this FortiSwitch PIM implementation.

choices.text: Apply the required advanced-features license
choices.feedback: PIM routing requires the advanced-features license.

questions.question: The multicast source and receiver are IPv6-only. Which conclusion matches FortiSwitchOS 8.0 PIM support?

choices.text: This PIM implementation is IPv4-only
choices.feedback: The guide lists IPv6 as unsupported for this PIM feature.

choices.text: Translate the IPv6 group into an IGMPv3 range
choices.feedback: IGMPv3 group-range configuration does not translate IPv6 multicast into supported IPv4 routing.

choices.text: Enable SSM mapping on the switch
choices.feedback: SSM mapping is explicitly unsupported.

choices.text: Use the documented IPv6 PIM mode
choices.feedback: The documented FortiSwitch PIM implementation does not provide IPv6 support.

questions.question: A client must keep its IP while roaming between APs managed by different controllers and different subnets. Which design applies?

choices.text: Tunnel-mode SSID with inter-controller mobility tunnel
choices.feedback: The mobility tunnel carries the Layer-3 roaming context across controllers.

choices.text: A second DHCP scope on the original controller
choices.feedback: A DHCP scope does not preserve the client's active IP during roaming.

choices.text: Bridge-mode SSID with identical VLAN IDs only
choices.feedback: Identical VLAN IDs alone do not create a cross-controller L3 handoff.

choices.text: 802.11k neighbor reports without controller coordination
choices.feedback: Neighbor reports assist client choice but do not transfer controller context.

questions.question: A roaming client keeps its original address while active, then receives a new subnet address after remaining idle. What explains this?

choices.text: The SSID encryption method changed during roaming
choices.feedback: Encryption changes do not explain the documented idle rehome behavior.

choices.text: The mobility tunnel failed and then recovered
choices.feedback: A tunnel failure is not the expected controlled transition after an idle timer.

choices.text: A client radio-band change triggered the move
choices.feedback: Band changes alone do not trigger the documented Layer-3 rehome timer.

choices.text: The client-idle rehome timer expired
choices.feedback: After the idle timer, the client is rehomed and receives an address on the new subnet.

questions.question: A deployment uses bridge-mode SSIDs across different subnets and expects the documented tunnel-mode L3 roaming behavior. What must change?

choices.text: Enable 802.11v steering on both controller groups
choices.feedback: 802.11v helps client steering, not cross-controller IP preservation.

choices.text: Disable DHCP on both controllers and AP groups
choices.feedback: Disabling DHCP does not provide the required mobility forwarding context.

choices.text: Reuse the gateway address across both subnets
choices.feedback: Duplicate gateways across separate subnets do not create a mobility tunnel.

choices.text: Use tunnel mode for the inter-controller L3 roam
choices.feedback: Fortinet documents inter-controller Layer-3 roaming for tunnel-mode SSIDs.

questions.question: The SSID name matches on both controllers, but the client loses sessions during movement. What should be verified first?

choices.text: Verify the mobility tunnel and matching tunnel-mode SSID
choices.feedback: The tunnel and matching SSID mode provide the documented handoff path.

choices.text: Compare radio channel width across both AP groups
choices.feedback: Channel width can affect RF performance but not the Layer-3 handoff mechanism.

choices.text: Check DHCP lease duration on the source controller
choices.feedback: Lease duration does not establish inter-controller forwarding context.

choices.text: Check the client profile's saved network name
choices.feedback: A saved SSID name proves only client-side network selection.

questions.question: A guest submits the self-registration form and immediately sees 'The input is required'. What should be checked first?

choices.text: The FortiSwitch native VLAN on every access port
choices.feedback: The error occurs in the portal workflow before switch VLAN enforcement.

choices.text: The guest account's final production VLAN
choices.feedback: The production VLAN is assigned later in the guest lifecycle.

choices.text: The sponsor's LDAP password expiration only
choices.feedback: Sponsor password expiry is not the documented missing-field cause.

choices.text: The Self Registration message-template assignments
choices.feedback: The documented scenario is caused by missing guest self-registration message templates.

questions.question: A sponsor never receives a self-registration request email. Which eligibility check is most relevant?

choices.text: The FortiGate has a route to the registration portal
choices.feedback: Portal routing may affect reachability but not sponsor account eligibility.

choices.text: The guest browser supports the required portal protocol
choices.feedback: Browser protocol support does not grant sponsor approval rights.

choices.text: The endpoint has adequate wireless signal strength
choices.feedback: RF signal does not determine sponsor notification eligibility.

choices.text: A permitted sponsor admin has a valid email address
choices.feedback: The sponsor must be a valid admin with self-registration permission and a usable email address.

questions.question: A guest request remains pending and expires before approval. Which setting directly controls this window?

choices.text: The account template's password complexity
choices.feedback: Password complexity does not control request expiry.

choices.text: The portal Guest Request Expiration value
choices.feedback: Guest Request Expiration sets how long the pending request remains valid.

choices.text: The FortiGate captive portal idle timeout
choices.feedback: The FortiGate idle timeout is not FortiNAC's request-expiration control.

choices.text: The guest's DHCP lease duration
choices.feedback: DHCP lease time is separate from the pending approval request timer.

questions.question: Credentials are delivered and the guest logs in, but the endpoint remains on the registration network. What evidence is next?

choices.text: Inspect the sponsor mailbox delivery and storage status
choices.feedback: Mailbox delivery is already complete; it does not prove network enforcement changed.

choices.text: Review the portal branding and registration page title
choices.feedback: Portal branding does not prove the host's access state changed.

choices.text: Verify host state, access policy and VLAN transition
choices.feedback: The final step is proving FortiNAC moved the host into production access.

choices.text: Check the email template's subject and sender address
choices.feedback: The email template does not determine the endpoint's network placement.

questions.question: FortiNAC-F sends CoA but the FortiSwitch rejects the request. Which AVPs are central to the documented FortiSwitch action?

choices.text: Framed-IP-Address and Acct-Interim-Interval only
choices.feedback: Those attributes support other RADIUS functions but do not specify the documented port action.

choices.text: Tunnel-Private-Group-ID and NAS-Port-Type only
choices.feedback: Those attributes can describe VLAN or NAS context but not the FortiSwitch CoA action.

choices.text: Calling-Station-Id and Fortinet-Host-Port-AVPair
choices.feedback: Calling-Station-Id identifies the host and the vendor AVPair specifies reauth or bounce.

choices.text: User-Name and Reply-Message only
choices.feedback: User-Name and Reply-Message do not express the required FortiSwitch port operation.

questions.question: A FortiSwitch returns CoA-ACK and reauthenticates the host, but the expected DACL is absent. Where should the DACL be returned?

choices.text: In the next RADIUS Access-Accept after reauthentication
choices.feedback: The subsequent Access-Accept carries the new authorization attributes such as DACL.

choices.text: Inside the RFC5176 CoA action attribute
choices.feedback: The CoA request triggers reauthentication; it is not the DACL response packet.

choices.text: In the FortiNAC device discovery poll
choices.feedback: Device discovery polling does not deliver RADIUS authorization attributes.

choices.text: In the DHCP Option 82 circuit identifier
choices.feedback: Option 82 identifies DHCP relay context, not the post-CoA DACL.

questions.question: A wired switch port has multiple hosts, including a daisy-chained phone and workstation. Which control selects the matching RFC5176 behavior?

choices.text: Use the device-level base group for every port
choices.feedback: The base group does not distinguish the documented multi-host conditions.

choices.text: Disable logical-network enforcement on the switch
choices.feedback: Disabling enforcement removes the context needed for logical-network overrides.

choices.text: Send a Disconnect-Request to every connected host
choices.feedback: A blanket disconnect does not select the correct per-port multi-host action.

choices.text: Set Multiple Connection and Daisy Chain RFC5176 behaviors
choices.feedback: FortiNAC-F has separate Multiple Connection and Daisy Chain settings for wired ports.

questions.question: A logical-network-specific CoA profile is configured, but a host remains on its current network and uses the base settings. Why?

choices.text: The override activates when the host enters that network
choices.feedback: The logical-network settings are applied when the host is switching to that network.

choices.text: The host needs a second MAC address to qualify
choices.feedback: A second MAC address is not required for logical-network selection.

choices.text: Logical-network settings always override device settings
choices.feedback: The override is conditional on the host transitioning to the configured logical network.

choices.text: The device must use UDP 1812 for CoA
choices.feedback: The documented RFC5176 receiver port defaults to 3799, not authentication port 1812.

questions.question: The FortiToken Mobile transfer option is unavailable on an air-gapped FortiAuthenticator. What is the expected limitation?

choices.text: The token must be changed from TOTP to HOTP
choices.feedback: TOTP/HOTP selection does not enable the online transfer service.

choices.text: Offline provisioning does not support transfer or push
choices.feedback: Offline mode does not support token transfer or push features.

choices.text: The user must be assigned to a TACACS group
choices.feedback: TACACS group membership is unrelated to mobile token transfer eligibility.

choices.text: The FortiGate must enable BFD on its WAN
choices.feedback: BFD is a routing liveness protocol, not a token transfer prerequisite.

questions.question: Transfer fails with 'unable to get local issuer certificate' while sending the activation email. What is the targeted repair?

choices.text: Increase the RADIUS accounting interim interval
choices.feedback: Accounting intervals do not affect SMTP certificate validation.

choices.text: Reassign the user's token to a different realm
choices.feedback: Realm reassignment does not repair the SMTP TLS certificate chain.

choices.text: Import the SMTP root and intermediate CA certificates
choices.feedback: The error indicates the SMTP server certificate chain is not trusted by FortiAuthenticator.

choices.text: Disable SMTP TLS verification on the appliance
choices.feedback: Disabling validation weakens the trust boundary and is not the documented repair.

questions.question: A token transfer completes on the new phone. What should the administrator expect on the old phone?

choices.text: The old device receives a second activation QR
choices.feedback: The new device uses the activation code; the old token is removed after completion.

choices.text: The transferred token is removed from the old device
choices.feedback: Successful transfer removes the old-device token.

choices.text: Both copies remain active until next login
choices.feedback: The transfer process does not leave two active copies as its final state.

choices.text: The old token changes automatically to an offline seed
choices.feedback: Offline provisioning is a separate mode and is not the transfer result.

questions.question: A remote-user synchronization rule assigns FortiToken Mobile while an administrator attempts to switch provisioning to Offline. What should be considered?

choices.text: The token sync rule can block Offline provisioning
choices.feedback: The documented dependency can prevent selecting Offline mode while this token assignment rule exists.

choices.text: The sync rule should use a TACACS-only profile
choices.feedback: TACACS is not the relevant synchronization setting.

choices.text: The RADIUS client subnet must be widened first
choices.feedback: Client subnet scope does not resolve the token provisioning dependency.

choices.text: Offline mode is required before any token transfer
choices.feedback: Offline mode does not support transfer and is not required for it.

questions.question: A privileged SSH operator should run only commands explicitly listed in the profile. Which mode matches that requirement?

choices.text: Deny mode with a short blocked-command list
choices.feedback: Deny mode blocks listed commands but leaves other commands permitted.

choices.text: Non-proxy mode with direct SSH access
choices.feedback: Non-proxy mode does not support SSH filters.

choices.text: Allow mode with only approved command patterns
choices.feedback: Allow mode permits listed patterns and blocks other shell commands.

choices.text: Logging-only mode with no command patterns
choices.feedback: Logging-only mode records activity without enforcing an allowlist.

questions.question: A shell allowlist works, but users can still open SFTP and port forwarding. What control is missing?

choices.text: Increase the secret's password expiration interval
choices.feedback: Password expiry does not restrict channels in an active SSH session.

choices.text: Block SFTP and forwarding channels separately
choices.feedback: FortiPAM has separate channel-block controls for SFTP and forwarding.

choices.text: Add more regular expressions for shell commands
choices.feedback: Shell regexes do not control non-shell SSH channel requests.

choices.text: Enable recording for every privileged SSH session
choices.feedback: Recording provides evidence but does not block SFTP or forwarding channels.

questions.question: A secret has an SSH filter attached, but commands pass without restriction. Which launch-path condition should be checked?

choices.text: The secret is using proxy mode
choices.feedback: SSH filters operate on the proxied SSH session; non-proxy mode bypasses them.

choices.text: The user's browser allows third-party cookies
choices.feedback: Browser cookies do not control native proxied SSH filtering.

choices.text: The video disk has free space
choices.feedback: Video storage affects recording, not the SSH command enforcement path.

choices.text: The target server has a static route
choices.feedback: Routing may affect reachability but not whether the filter is applied.

questions.question: SSH commands appear in the event log but cannot be linked to Web SSH video playback. What limitation applies?

choices.text: Limit commands to fewer than eight characters
choices.feedback: Command length is not the documented association boundary.

choices.text: Require Deny mode for command-to-video correlation
choices.feedback: Deny mode is not required for command/video association.

choices.text: Agentless Web SSH cannot link SSH events to video
choices.feedback: FortiPAM documents that agentless Web SSH cannot associate SSH log events with video.

choices.text: Change the secret's target port for video linkage
choices.feedback: Target port selection does not remove the agentless-mode limitation.

questions.question: Kubernetes posts to the webhook endpoint but the collector does not parse events. Which credential detail should be verified?

choices.text: The Windows agent polling interval on the host
choices.feedback: Agent polling is a separate ingestion path, not this push webhook.

choices.text: The webhook receiver port and endpoint path mapping
choices.feedback: The receiver port and path affect reachability, not event-payload parsing.

choices.text: Newline separator with EventList JSON framing
choices.feedback: The documented credential uses a newline separator and Kubernetes audit EventList JSON.

choices.text: The Kubernetes audit API version and namespace
choices.feedback: API version and namespace do not replace the required EventList payload framing.

questions.question: Kubernetes rejects the FortiSIEM webhook during TLS validation. What collector prerequisite is documented?

choices.text: An expired certificate pinned in the sender
choices.feedback: An expired certificate cannot satisfy normal TLS validation.

choices.text: A self-signed certificate with no chain
choices.feedback: The guide warns that webhook senders validate the receiver certificate chain.

choices.text: A wildcard certificate without a trusted issuer
choices.feedback: A wildcard name alone does not establish trust without a valid chain.

choices.text: A public CA-signed TLS certificate on the receiver
choices.feedback: The collector must present a public CA-signed certificate trusted by the sender.

questions.question: The webhook credential is saved, but Kubernetes cannot reach the endpoint on the intended collector. What should be checked?

choices.text: The Supervisor's time zone display format only
choices.feedback: Time-zone display does not determine the receiver address.

choices.text: The FortiSIEM report template and color settings
choices.feedback: Report styling does not determine webhook endpoint routing.

choices.text: The incident rule's severity and notification threshold
choices.feedback: Incident severity does not control endpoint deployment.

choices.text: Receiver FQDN and Save and Deploy target
choices.feedback: The endpoint is generated from the receiver FQDN and deployed to the selected node.

questions.question: The sender supports HMAC signing, but FortiSIEM is configured for Basic Auth. What is the best correction?

choices.text: Replace the receiver FQDN with a node IP everywhere
choices.feedback: The hostname should remain consistent with the certificate and endpoint configuration.

choices.text: Change the Kubernetes audit API version to v1beta1
choices.feedback: The sample uses audit.k8s.io/v1; changing API versions does not fix auth mismatch.

choices.text: Select the same supported authentication method on both sides
choices.feedback: The sender and FortiSIEM credential must agree on Basic Auth, HMAC or Simple Secret.

choices.text: Disable webhook authentication on both sides
choices.feedback: Disabling authentication is unnecessary and weakens the integration.

questions.question: RBI is absent from the FortiSASE GUI on a new instance. Which prerequisite set should be checked first?

choices.text: Confirm availability, subscription, Security PoP and proxy enablement
choices.feedback: RBI requires feature availability, an eligible subscription, supported Security PoP and proxy enabled.

choices.text: SAML group membership for the selected SWG policy
choices.feedback: SAML group membership affects user assignment but not initial feature availability.

choices.text: The number of active VPN tunnels on the instance
choices.feedback: VPN tunnel count is not the RBI feature eligibility gate.

choices.text: The endpoint browser version and local cache
choices.feedback: Browser version does not enable the instance-level feature entitlement.

questions.question: Isolated browsing suddenly fails for every user after heavy use. Which limit best explains the shared outage?

choices.text: One endpoint reached its five-session limit
choices.feedback: A per-endpoint session limit affects that endpoint, not all users.

choices.text: A single user's browser cache is full
choices.feedback: A local cache problem is not an instance-wide isolation control.

choices.text: The instance-wide isolation data quota was exceeded
choices.feedback: FortiSASE documents that quota exhaustion blocks isolated traffic for all users.

choices.text: One proxy policy has too many URL entries
choices.feedback: Policy size does not explain a global isolation-data block.

questions.question: One endpoint cannot start another isolated session while other users continue working. What should be inspected?

choices.text: The endpoint's concurrent RBI session limit
choices.feedback: RBI limits concurrent sessions per endpoint, with a documented default of five.

choices.text: The instance-wide RBI entitlement and subscription
choices.feedback: An instance entitlement is shared; it does not explain a single endpoint's concurrency cap.

choices.text: The selected proxy policy's URL category rule
choices.feedback: URL category rules govern which sites are isolated, not the endpoint session count.

choices.text: The Security PoP's current RBI service status
choices.feedback: PoP availability would affect a broader user set, not one endpoint's session limit.

questions.question: An SWG SSO deployment has RBI issues around the CSP_REPORT proxy policy. Which inspection mode is documented?

choices.text: Apply deep inspection to every CSP_REPORT request
choices.feedback: Deep inspection is not the documented setting for this policy path.

choices.text: Remove certificate inspection and the proxy policy
choices.feedback: Removing the proxy policy breaks the RBI/SWG path rather than fixing it.

choices.text: Certificate inspection for the CSP_REPORT security profile
choices.feedback: Fortinet specifies certificate inspection rather than deep inspection for the CSP_REPORT profile.

choices.text: Use endpoint-side TLS decryption for this profile
choices.feedback: Endpoint-side decryption is not the FortiSASE proxy-policy requirement.

questions.question: Both WAN members are reachable, but the voice SLA fails on one path. Which output distinguishes reachability from voice eligibility?

choices.text: The route's administrative distance only
choices.feedback: Distance ranks routes and does not show the MOS target result.

choices.text: The interface administrative state only
choices.feedback: Administrative state proves local interface status, not voice quality.

choices.text: The health-check MOS and SLA map
choices.feedback: MOS and the SLA map show whether the member passes the voice metric.

choices.text: The DNS cache entry for the SIP registrar
choices.feedback: DNS cache state does not show the path's measured voice SLA.

questions.question: The MOS score changes materially after selecting G.722 instead of G.729. What explains the change?

choices.text: MOS calculation depends on the selected codec
choices.feedback: The theoretical maximum and score depend on the selected voice codec.

choices.text: The policy stopped matching the voice application
choices.feedback: Policy matching does not explain a codec-specific calculated score change.

choices.text: The SD-WAN member's IP address changed
choices.feedback: The member address is not the codec input to the MOS formula.

choices.text: The health-check server was automatically replaced
choices.feedback: The guide does not describe codec selection as changing the server.

questions.question: A MOS threshold is failing, but the service rule uses priority mode. Why might traffic not steer by MOS?

choices.text: The health-check server must use ICMP only
choices.feedback: MOS calculation supports the configured health-check measurement and codec options.

choices.text: MOS cannot steer when the service mode is priority
choices.feedback: Fortinet documents that MOS cannot steer traffic in priority mode; use an SLA-capable mode.

choices.text: The member must be removed from the SD-WAN zone
choices.feedback: The member can remain in the zone while failing its SLA.

choices.text: The MOS codec must be set to a custom value
choices.feedback: Only the documented G.711, G.729 or G.722 codecs are supported.

questions.question: Packet loss is zero but the MOS score is below target. Which interpretation is correct?

choices.text: The route is necessarily missing from the table
choices.feedback: A low MOS score does not by itself prove a missing route.

choices.text: Latency, jitter and codec can still lower MOS
choices.feedback: Latency and jitter still affect the codec-aware MOS calculation.

choices.text: The health-check must be disabled and recreated
choices.feedback: Recreating the check is not indicated without examining its measurements.

choices.text: Zero loss proves the voice SLA must pass
choices.feedback: MOS uses multiple inputs; zero loss alone does not prove voice quality.

questions.question: FortiNAC-F receives a CoA-ACK, but the host's new DACL is absent. Which transaction boundary is most likely misunderstood?

choices.text: The CoA request should carry the final DACL
choices.feedback: The CoA request asks the NAS to act; it is not the final DACL response.

choices.text: The FortiSwitch should skip reauthentication after CoA
choices.feedback: The documented workflow reauthenticates the session to receive updated authorization.

choices.text: The RADIUS server should place DACL in CoA-ACK
choices.feedback: CoA-ACK acknowledges the action; the updated DACL is delivered in the subsequent Access-Accept.

choices.text: The DACL arrives in the next Access-Accept
choices.feedback: The subsequent Access-Accept carries the new VLAN or DACL attributes.

questions.question: FortiGate and FortiSandbox logs arrive at FortiAnalyzer, but analysts cannot build one combined report. Which first check is most targeted?

choices.text: Whether both devices share the same Fabric ADOM
choices.feedback: The Fabric ADOM is the shared analysis scope for cross-product views and reports.

choices.text: Whether FortiGate uses BFD for its default route
choices.feedback: BFD does not determine FortiAnalyzer report scope.

choices.text: Whether FortiPAM SSH filters are in Allow mode
choices.feedback: PAM command filters do not affect FortiAnalyzer ADOM membership.

choices.text: Whether Kubernetes webhook authentication uses HMAC signing
choices.feedback: Webhook authentication is unrelated to the two devices' ADOM placement.
